title: Heracles: Death and Apotheosis
subtitle: A centaur's revenge, a burning robe, and a seat among the gods

learningObjectives.text: What happens to him after death?

main.author: Pseudo-Apollodorus
main.locator: Library 2.7.7, the pyre and reception among the gods; book 2 · chapter 7 · section 7, normalized characters 2438-2965
main.excerpt: he came of age, proceeded to Mount Oeta, in the Trachinian territory, and there constructed a pyre, mounted it, and gave orders to kindle it. When no one would do so, Poeas, passing by to look for his flocks, set a light to it. On him Hercules bestowed his bow. While the pyre was burning, it is said that a cloud passed under Hercules and with a peal of thunder wafted him up to heaven. Thereafter he obtained immortality, and being reconciled to Hera he married her daughter Hebe, by whom he had sons, Alexiares and Anicetus.

narrativeBlocks.title: The centaur's dying gift
narrativeBlocks.body: Years before, the centaur Nessus tried to assault Heracles's wife Deianira; Heracles shot him. Dying, Nessus told Deianira his blood was a love charm — keep it, and Heracles will never stray. She kept it.

narrativeBlocks.title: The robe of fire
narrativeBlocks.body: When Deianira fears a rival, she soaks a robe in the centaur's blood and sends it to Heracles. It is poisoned: the fabric burns into his skin and cannot be torn off without tearing his flesh with it. The greatest body in the world dies by his wife's desperate gift.

narrativeBlocks.title: The pyre on Oeta
narrativeBlocks.body: In agony beyond bearing, Heracles builds his own pyre on Mount Oeta and lies on it. No one will light the fire until a passing stranger does — the strongest man in creation begging for a mercy burn.

narrativeBlocks.title: Up, not down
narrativeBlocks.body: The flames take the mortal part — and the immortal part ascends to Olympus. Hera finally relents; Heracles marries Hebe, goddess of youth, and feasts with the gods. He is the only hero in the whole cycle who becomes a god.

narrativeBlocks.title: A hero's strange ending
narrativeBlocks.body: The apotheosis is earned the hard way — no other hero buys divinity with a life this painful. The Greeks meant it as the final verdict: the labours were redemption enough to lift him above mortals.
